title: the merge-driver install proof asserts the driver string and dry-run output as they are on Windows, not as they print on Linux
intention: the merge-driver install proof builds and asserts the driver string as the artifact tool writes it (shell-quoted) and reaches the dry run's output through a red step, so it passes on Windows and on Linux.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: on akiendell the proof ran 3 of 5 red: tooth 2 (unquoted PYTHONPATH expected), tooth 3 (backslashes stripped in the stale string), tooth 5 (dry run prints only reds)
traces_to: Law 3: the proof asserted a form never measured on this box; Law 8: a proof that reds on a correct build is not trusted either way.
how: In the proof: quote the repo path with shlex.quote in tooth 2's assertion and tooth 3's stale string, read the interpreter with shlex.split, and in tooth 5 aim the artifact tool's roots at an unconfigured scratch repo so the dry run prints [OFFERED] journal-merge-driver. No installer change.

clauses.claim: the proof runs green on akiendell, twice, all five teeth
the proof still reds if the installer stops laying the driver (a hollow build fails the teeth)
